headline: Approved September minutes and heard KPMG audit results; no major decisions were made.
summary: The commission heard results of a KPMG audit and held an executive session on related findings. Members also asked about the city's AI policy, and the general manager said a city-wide policy was released in September 2026. The commission approved the September 9, 2026 minutes by a 4-0 vote.
decisions: Approved the September 9, 2026 minutes with a typo correction, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Vota moved to accept the September 9, 2026 minutes pending the typo correction; Commissioner Williams seconded the motion. Vote: 4 ayes 0 nays.

plain_text:
1 
 
 
 
DRAFT 
MINUTES OF REGULAR MEETING 
BURLINGTON ELECTRIC COMMISSION 
 
Wednesday, October 14, 2026 
                  
The regular meeting of the Burlington Electric Commission was convened at 5:02 p.m. on 
Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at Burlington Electric Department, 585 Pine Street, Burlington, 
Vermont, and on Microsoft Teams. 
 
Attendance 
• Channel 17 was present to record this meeting. 
• Commissioners Paul Dawson, Ali Kenney, Andy Vota, and Brian Willams were present at 
585 Pine Street.  
• Staff members Paul Alexander, Sami Bousnina, Amanda Hurlbut, Mike Kanarick, Munir 
Kasti, Katie Morris, Darren Springer, and Emily Stebbins-Wheelock were present at 585 
Pine Street. 
• Staff member James Gibbons was present via Microsoft Teams.  
• Public members Leendert Huisman and Peter Macausland were present at 585 Pine Street. 
• Public members Jake Day and Jeffrey Koch of KPMG were present via Microsoft Teams.  
 
1. Agenda 
There were no changes to the agenda.  
 
2. Meeting Minutes 
There was one proposed change to correct a typo to “Velerity” in the September 9, 2026 minutes.  
 
Commissioner Vota moved to accept the September 9, 2026 minutes pending the typo correction; 
Commissioner Williams seconded the motion. Vote: 4 ayes 0 nays.  
 
3. Public Forum 
Peter Macausland addressed the commission noting the importance of detailed minutes outlining 
points that were discussed in the meeting so that other public members can benefit from the 
discussion.  
 
Leendert Huisman addressed the commission regarding the Velerity report.  
 
4. KPMG Audit Presentation 
Amanda Hurlbut, BED Controller, Jake Day, and Jeffrey Koch of KPMG presented the results of the 
KPMG audit.
2 
 
 
 
Commissioner Vota moved that the commission enter executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. statute 
313(a)(3) for the purpose of discussing the evaluation of public employees in connection with 
findings and recommendations contained in the KPMG audit; Commissioner Dawson seconded the 
motion. Vote 4 aye 0 nay. The Burlington Electric Commission entered executive session at 5:24 
p.m.  
 
Commissioner Vota made a motion to exit executive session; Commissioner Williams seconded the 
motion. Vote 4 aye 0 nay. The Burlington Electric Commission exited executive session at 5:41 p.m.  
 
5. Monthly Impact Minute 
Emily Stebbins-Wheelock, CFO and Manager of Strategy and Innovation, introduced Sami Bousnina, 
BED’s new Financial Analyst.  
 
6. Commissioners’ Corner 
Commissioner Williams asked about the use of AI and if there was a city policy regarding AI use 
within City departments.  
 
General Manager Darren Springer responded that the city recently released a city-wide AI policy as 
of September 2026.  
 
7. GM Update 
General Manager Darren Springer gave a monthly update.  
 
8. Financials: August FY27 
Emily Stebbins-Wheelock, CFO and Manager of Strategy & Innovation, presented August 2026 
financial results. 
 
9. Commissioners’ Check-In 
There were no topics discussed.  
 
Adjourn  
Commissioner Dawson made a motion to adjourn; the motion was seconded by Commissioner 
Williams. Vote: 4 ayes 0 nays. 
 
The meeting of the Burlington Electric Commission adjourned at 6:08 p.m. 
 
Microsoft Teams transcript used to draft minutes prepared by Katie Morris and edited by Emily 
Stebbins-Wheelock, CFO and Manager of Strategy & Innovation.
